title: LA-ICPMS Analysis Detail
description: Detail block for LA-ICP-MS hasPart items. Discriminates on ada:componentType, carries analysis-level required properties and an @id reference to a registered laicpmsTAPP definition, and per-dataset schema:additionalProperty entries constrained via $refs to the parameterValues registry plus a catch-all. Generated by tools/build_tapp.py.

schema:measurementTechnique.description: @id reference to a registered laicpmsTAPP TAPP definition.

ada:analyst.description: Name(s) of the analyst(s) who performed the actual analysis. ORCID is recommended for persistent identification.

ada:analysisStartDate.description: Date on which the analytical session began. For analyses spanning multiple days, use the date of the first session. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

ada:analysisEndDate.description: Date on which the analytical session ended. May equal Analysis Start Date for single-day sessions. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

ada:fundingSourceForAnalysis.description: Grants and other funding sources that supported the specific sample analyses and data collection reported here. Include grant numbers and funding agencies. Distinct from protocol development funding, which may have been awarded years earlier.

ada:sampleName.description: Name or identifier of the sample analysed, as used in the laboratory. Should match the identifier used in associated publications or data tables.

ada:oxideProduction.description: Actual oxide production ratio measured during this analytical session, using the method specified in the protocol-level field "Oxide Production Method and Threshold". Report the measured value and confirm it met the protocol threshold.

ada:analysisLocationSpotCoordinates.description: Location of the analysis on the sample surface. For spot and transect analysis: stage coordinates (X, Y in µm) or a description relative to a named reference feature (e.g., mineral rim, inclusion boundary). For mapping: coordinates of the map corner(s) or centre, plus map dimensions. Enables spatial reconstruction and co-registration with other analytical images.

ada:numberOfReplicates.description: Number of replicate analyses performed on the same sample (or same nominal location for spot analysis) in this session. For spot analysis: number of individual spot analyses per grain or location. For transect: number of replicate transect lines. For mapping: number of map acquisitions of the same area (usually 1).

ada:transectLength.description: Total length of the transect line analysed in micrometres. This is an analysis-level parameter because it depends on the size of the feature of interest rather than being fixed in the protocol. The protocol fixes scan speed (captured in Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size); transect length is determined at analysis time based on grain or feature size.

ada:mappingArea.description: Total area covered by the 2D raster map, expressed as width × height in µm or as total area in µm² or mm². This is an analysis-level parameter because it depends on the size of the grain or phase to be mapped. The protocol fixes scan speed, line spacing, and spot size; the map area is chosen at analysis time to cover the target feature.

ada:signalIntegrationTime.description: Actual integration time used for the ablation signal in this analysis, in seconds. This is an analysis-level outcome determined during data reduction by applying the Signal Integration Interval Method to the time-resolved signal. It is equal to or shorter than the Ablation Duration per Spot because the signal start and end transients are typically discarded. Not applicable to mapping analysis: for mapping, the equivalent concept is the per-pixel cycle time, which is determined by the spectrometer dwell time settings (a protocol-level field) rather than being an analysis-level outcome.

anyOf.title: Coupled Technique(s)
anyOf.description: Analytical technique(s) applied to the same sample or aliquot in conjunction with this protocol, where the two analyses are designed to be interpreted together or where one provides input to the other. Use the same controlled vocabulary as the Technique field. Enter "None" if no coupling is intended.

anyOf.title: Coupling Description
anyOf.description: Description of how this protocol is coupled with the technique(s) listed above. Include: (1) the functional relationship — what data or context flows between techniques or how results are combined (e.g., which output from the coupled technique serves as input to data reduction for this technique); and (2) the analytical sequence — which technique is performed first and why (e.g., non-destructive before destructive).

anyOf.title: Coupled Protocol DOI
anyOf.description: Registered protocol DOI for the coupled technique named above. Provides a stable, citable link to the companion method independent of whether a dataset has been deposited. If the coupled protocol has not yet been registered, enter the DOI of a publication describing the coupled method, or "pending". Enter "None" if no coupling is planned.

anyOf.title: Coupled Dataset or Publication Reference
anyOf.description: DOI or other persistent identifier for the co-registered dataset or publication where both datasets are reported together. Accepts: a dedicated dataset DOI (if separately deposited), a shared dataset DOI (if co-submitted in the same package), or a publication DOI. Use "same submission" if the coupled dataset is included in this data package, or "pending" if not yet assigned. If coupling is documented through a shared sample identifier only, that information is already captured in Sample Persistent Identifier (Group 2).

anyOf.title: Sample Form / Analytical Substrate
anyOf.description: Physical form of the material as it enters the ablation cell. Editable to accommodate legitimate variations (e.g., thin section vs. mount) that do not alter the analytical protocol.

anyOf.title: Sample Persistent Identifier
anyOf.description: Globally unique, persistent identifier for the analysed sample. IGSN (International Geo Sample Number) is the recommended standard for geological and cosmochemical samples, as used by Astromat, EarthChem, and SESAR.

anyOf.title: Fusion Flux and Dilution Ratio
anyOf.description: For protocols using fused glass, the flux type and sample:flux dilution ratio used to prepare the analytical glass.

anyOf.title: Sample Preparation Method
anyOf.description: Description of how samples were prepared for analysis (mounting, polishing, coating, fusion procedure, etc.).

anyOf.title: Pre-Ablation Surface Treatment
anyOf.description: Protocol applied immediately before each analysis to remove surface contamination or condition the sample surface. Distinct from general sample preparation. For spot analysis, pre-ablation pulses are discarded before signal acquisition begins. For mapping, this step is typically omitted as the large area ablated averages out surface effects.

anyOf.title: Torch Depth
anyOf.description: Distance between the load coil and the sampling cone tip (mm), also called injector depth or torch position depending on the instrument manufacturer. Affects ion transmission efficiency, oxide formation, and doubly-charged species production. The protocol specifies a target value optimised during initial setup; the analyst confirms or fine-adjusts during session tuning.

anyOf.title: Mass Resolution Setting
anyOf.description: Operating mass resolution of the mass analyser. For quadrupole instruments this is fixed at unit resolution by instrument design. For sector-field instruments the analyst selects low, medium, or high resolution to balance sensitivity against spectral interference suppression.

anyOf.title: Acquisition Software
anyOf.description: Instrument control and data acquisition software used to collect raw signal data, including version number. Separate from data reduction software.

anyOf.title: Data Reduction Software
anyOf.description: Software used for signal processing, background subtraction, and concentration calculation, including version number.

anyOf.title: Laser Spot Geometry
anyOf.description: Shape and dimensions of the laser ablation spot in micrometres registered by the protocol. For circular spots, report diameter; for square or rectangular spots, report width × length. The protocol registers the typical geometry; analysts may adjust within protocol-allowed range.

anyOf.title: Laser Energy
anyOf.description: Laser pulse energy in millijoules as set at the laser output or measured at the sample surface. Less commonly reported than fluence because it does not account for spot area. Report only when the system displays energy directly. Laser fluence (J cm⁻²) is the preferred quantity and is captured in Default Laser Fluence.

anyOf.title: Laser Fluence (Energy Density)
anyOf.description: Laser pulse energy per unit area at the sample surface in J cm⁻², as registered by the protocol. Fluence is the physically meaningful quantity controlling ablation rate, crater morphology, elemental fractionation, and particle size distribution. If the system reports only as % of maximum output, include that value and note the system maximum where known.

anyOf.title: Laser Repetition Rate
anyOf.description: Laser pulse repetition rate in hertz registered by the protocol. For mapping methods, repetition rate together with scan speed and spot size determines pixel size and spatial resolution. Analysts may adjust within protocol-allowed bounds.

anyOf.title: Ablation Duration per Spot
anyOf.description: Total on-sample ablation (signal acquisition) time per individual spot in seconds, as set in the acquisition method. This is a protocol-level parameter for spot analysis: it reflects the deliberate trade-off between signal accumulation (longer = lower LOD), sample consumption, and session throughput. For transect analysis, the equivalent protocol-level parameter is scan speed (captured in Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size). For mapping analysis, total acquisition time is sample-area-dependent and therefore analysis-level, not captured here.

anyOf.title: Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size
anyOf.description: For continuous line scan (transect) and raster mapping: the stage translation speed in µm s⁻¹. This is the protocol-level parameter that, together with spot size and repetition rate, determines spatial resolution along the scan direction. For mapping, the mapping rate (mm² h⁻¹) may be reported as an alternative when scan speed is session-variable. For stepped line profiles: the distance between successive spot positions in µm.

schema:name.const: Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size

anyOf.title: Raster Line Spacing (Mapping Only)
anyOf.description: Distance between adjacent raster lines in a 2D elemental map, measured perpendicular to the scan direction, in micrometres. Together with spot size, this determines whether adjacent lines are contiguous (line spacing = spot size), overlapping (line spacing < spot size), or have gaps (line spacing > spot size). Applies to raster mapping only.

anyOf.title: Carrier Gas and Flow Rate
anyOf.description: Gas used to transport ablated aerosol from the ablation cell to the ICP-MS torch, with the protocol-registered target flow rate(s). Helium is standard for most UV laser systems due to superior aerosol transport. Flow rates are protocol targets; actual session values may be adjusted within ±10% during tuning.

anyOf.title: Plasma / Make-up Gas Addition
anyOf.description: Additional gas(es) mixed into the carrier stream downstream of the ablation cell, with the protocol-registered target flow rate. Ar make-up gas is standard. Small N₂ additions can enhance sensitivity for some elements. If N₂ is not added, state "None" explicitly to distinguish from not reported.

anyOf.title: Auxiliary and Cool Gas Flow Rates
anyOf.description: ICP auxiliary (intermediate) and cool (outer/plasma) Ar gas flow rates in l min⁻¹. The protocol registers target values; actual session values may be adjusted slightly during tuning.

schema:name.const: Auxiliary and Cool Gas Flow Rates

anyOf.title: Signal Smoothing
anyOf.description: Description of any signal smoothing device or approach installed between the ablation cell and the ICP-MS to reduce pulse-to-pulse signal variability. Note: active signal smoothing devices (e.g., squid, SCFAST) are generally incompatible with high-resolution raster mapping because they degrade spatial resolution by mixing aerosol from successive laser shots. For mapping analyses, report "None" explicitly.

anyOf.title: ICP Tuning
anyOf.description: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria (e.g., oxide production threshold, sensitivity targets, mass calibration).

anyOf.title: Doubly-Charged Species Monitor
anyOf.description: The mass ratio monitored to estimate doubly-charged ion (M²⁺) formation during instrument tuning. Doubly-charged ions appear at half the mass of the parent ion and can cause isobaric interferences on analytes in that mass region. The monitor species and the mass positions monitored should be stated explicitly. Analogous to Oxide Production Method and Threshold for oxide monitoring.

anyOf.title: Doubly-Charged Species Production
anyOf.description: Measured percentage of doubly-charged ion production for the monitored species at the time of instrument tuning. The protocol should specify the acceptable threshold (e.g., <1%, <3%); the measured value for each session is recorded here. Report both the threshold and the measured value where possible.

anyOf.title: Drift Monitor Frequency
anyOf.description: Frequency at which primary reference materials are analysed to monitor instrument drift and apply drift corrections across the session. Editable to allow analysts to increase monitoring frequency if drift is observed.

anyOf.title: Analysis Sequence
anyOf.description: Repeating order of primary calibration standard(s), quality control standard(s), and unknown analyses within a measurement session. Editable to allow minor adjustments while maintaining the bracketing strategy defined in the protocol.

anyOf.title: Spectrometer Dwell Time
anyOf.description: Count time (dwell time) per mass position for each measured isotope in milliseconds. Longer dwell times improve counting statistics and lower detection limits but reduce the number of isotopes measurable within a given scan cycle time. For mapping, scan cycle time directly determines spatial resolution at a given scan speed: shorter cycle time = finer spatial resolution.

anyOf.title: Background Count Time
anyOf.description: Total time spent measuring gas blank (background signal with laser off or shutter closed) before each ablation event, in seconds. For spot and transect analysis, a discrete background interval is measured before each ablation. For mapping, background is typically measured once per raster line or at the start of a map session rather than before each individual pixel. Editable to allow session-specific adjustment.

anyOf.title: Uncertainty Propagation Method
anyOf.description: Approach used to propagate analytical uncertainty from raw count rates through the data reduction chain to final reported concentrations or isotope ratios. Specifies which uncertainty sources are included: counting statistics, calibration standard uncertainty, internal standard concentration uncertainty, drift correction uncertainty. Editable because this field may be unspecified at protocol registration (Advanced tier) and can be completed by the analyst when documenting the analysis.

anyOf.title: Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach
anyOf.description: Method used to identify and remove anomalous signal spikes arising from micronuggets, inclusions, cracks, or instrument artifacts during time-resolved signal processing. Editable because the specific implementation may vary between sessions while remaining within the protocol framework.

anyOf.title: Pulse/Analog Detector Nonlinearity Correction
anyOf.description: Whether a correction was applied for nonlinear response at the transition between pulse-counting and analog detector modes.

anyOf.title: Memory Effect Mitigation
anyOf.description: Protocol applied to identify and minimise memory effects from high-concentration elements in the previous sample or standard that may contaminate subsequent analyses, or from incomplete aerosol washout between adjacent pixels in raster mapping mode. For mapping, the mitigation strategy involves controlling scan speed relative to washout time to ensure each pixel signal is sufficiently free of the preceding pixel's contribution.

anyOf.title: Normalization / Standards-Based Correction
anyOf.description: Any post-acquisition normalization applied to correct for systematic biases identified from secondary reference materials, or stoichiometric normalization applied per pixel in mapping. Distinct from the primary internal standard approach captured in Internal Standard Approach.

anyOf.title: Primary Calibration Standard Name
anyOf.description: Primary reference material(s) used to calibrate the instrument and convert raw signal intensities to concentrations or isotope ratios. Include material name, source institution, and citation for the accepted values used. Editable because the specific lot or certification vintage may differ between sessions while the material type remains the same.

anyOf.title: Secondary Reference Materials
anyOf.description: Quality-control reference materials analysed as unknowns alongside samples in the same session to assess accuracy and monitor drift. Include material name, source, and citation for accepted values used for comparison. Editable because selection of secondary RMs may vary across sessions.

anyOf.title: Additional Notes
anyOf.description: Any additional context about this protocol or analysis session not captured by the structured fields above. Use sparingly; structured fields are preferred for all information that can be formally categorised.
Catch-all for additional schema:PropertyValue entries beyond the laicpmsTAPP-derived catalog.
